claim_form: Headroom in the England and Wales prison estate, as published in the Ministry of Justice weekly prison population bulletin for Monday {target}, will be {forecast}, with an 80% interval of {lower} to {upper}.
definition: Headroom means the bulletin's total-estate Useable Operational Capacity minus total-estate Population.

provenance.note: The register file is the source of truth. If this ledger and that file disagree, the file wins.

data_sources: MoJ weekly prison population bulletin, gov.uk, Prison population: weekly estate figures
Annual Statement on Prison Capacity 2025, published 29 January 2026

benchmarks.name: Seasonal naive
benchmarks.definition: 2,094 plus the mean seasonal change to the target week from the 2011 to 2026 weekly profile

benchmarks.name: Official path
benchmarks.definition: Adult-estate supply minus central demand from Figure 4, plus the YCS headroom at the base date (99). Published only where the Statement gives a dated point.
benchmarks.edition: Annual Statement on Prison Capacity 2025, 29 January 2026

scoring_rule: Field. Total-estate Useable Operational Capacity minus total-estate Population in the MoJ weekly bulletin, equal to the bulletin's own Headroom row. The figure as first published is used; later MoJ revisions are logged but do not change the score.

Resolving bulletin. The bulletin whose reference date equals the target date. If no bulletin exists for that date, the first bulletin after it resolves the line, and that bulletin's date is recorded as the resolving date.
Error equals forecast minus outcome, in people, sign kept.
Interval hit means the outcome falls within the 80% interval, inclusive.

Closer means a smaller absolute error than the named baseline, per line. Across the track, the model is said to beat a baseline only when its running mean absolute error is lower over at least 13 resolved lines.

Policy events between bulletins have no effect. A release tranche, a recall change, a capacity measure or anything else occurring between bulletins does not alter the forecast or the score. This is not a claim that policy does not matter: it is that a forecast which can be revised after the fact is not a forecast. Events are logged for context only.

Definitional change. If the MoJ changes the meaning of useable operational capacity, the line is still scored against the published figure and the change is logged. The target is the published number.
cadence: Marks happen when a target resolves, not weekly. Bulletins publish on Fridays for the preceding Monday. From Friday 11 September 2026 a new forecast is posted every bulletin week at 4, 13 and 26 weeks ahead, so the track gains three lines a week. The eight lines below are the founding set, not the cadence.
superseded_versions: Model versions v1 and v2 are retained in the register file and scored alongside v3. They are not shown here and are never deleted from the file.

lines.resolving_note: Bank holiday, substitute Boxing Day. Resolves against the next bulletin by rule 2.
Easter Monday. Resolves against the next bulletin by rule 2.
Spring bank holiday. Resolves against the next bulletin by rule 2.
